evidence: io.lisp:3414 `(position (fnn-log-rotate-now store))` is evaluated in the let* before the setup verdict. Later, at io.lisp:3447-3451: `((eq verdict :unencodable) (fnn-refuse "the recovered Store state is not encodable as a checkpoint")) ((and (consp verdict) (eq (first verdict) :deferred)) (fnn-refuse "checkpoint deferred reason=~(~a~) ..."))`. fnn-log-rotate-now (io.lisp:7418) runs `fnn-log-prepare-spare` (a new segment preallocated to `fn-store-log-initial-extent`), then `fnn-log-rotate` and `fnn-log-make-durable`.
fix: Ask ACL2 for the setup verdict (budget, free space, encodability) before rotating, and rotate only on a :plan. Otherwise make the rotation part of the program ACL2 admits, so a refusal leaves the log untouched.
reviewer: io.lisp:3414 binds position via fnn-log-rotate-now (io.lisp:7418-7423: prepare-spare, rotate, make-durable) before the :unencodable/:deferred refusals at io.lisp:3447-3451, so a refused checkpoint has already rotated the log and preallocated a segment of fn-store-log-initial-extent. The claim that fnn-log-drop never removes anything is overstated. fnn-log-covered-indices (io.lisp:7425) drops every segment present below the next successful checkpoint's first segment, so the extra segments are reclaimed then. segment-index-exhausted (io.lisp:7305) is a remote limit. What remains real is one initial extent of disk per refused attempt, spent while the deferral may be about free space.
scenario: An operator or script runs `store ROOT checkpoint` (or the operator wrapper at operator.lisp:643, or checkpoint.lisp:71/191) while the checkpoint budget or free space is too small. ACL2 answers (:deferred ...) and the command exits 1 with a refusal. By then the log has already rotated durably: it consumed a segment index and closed the old segment, and no checkpoint covers the new one, so fnn-log-drop never removes anything. Each retry adds another preallocated segment and moves toward `segment-index-exhausted`. The refused attempt also uses up the very disk space whose shortage caused the deferral. The same happens when the staged write fails with fnn-refuse-io after the rotation.
title: Offline checkpoint rotates the record log before ACL2 decides :deferred/:unencodable, so a refused checkpoint still rotates the log for good
